fit: historical oral lovage root use for pain and a separate leaf tea use
assessment: Two interview reports describe root decoction for joint pain and two leaf tea for inflammation. No dried-leaf pain response, comparator, or Parkinson diagnosis is reported.

fit: spearmint test odor in Parkinson and drug induced parkinsonism
assessment: The original reports less accurate spearmint odor recognition in 78 Parkinson participants versus 31 with drug-induced parkinsonism. The groups differed by age. The ingredient served as a test odor, with no brewed ingestion or treatment contrast.

fit: mint scent in a bundled olfactory training protocol
assessment: The protocol uses a mint label and conventional menthol stimulus among four odorants. The population has olfactory dysfunction and subjective cognitive decline. There is no independent mint arm, established culinary spearmint species or brewed preparation.

fit: standardized clove oil with rice bran oil and self reported cognitive failures
assessment: Cognitive Failures Questionnaire scores moved from 39 to 27 in the higher-dose arm (within p≤.005). The randomized design has two active doses and no placebo. Participants did not have Parkinson and the study does not isolate ground clove or objectively measured executive change.

fit: clove scent within four odorants and Trail Making cognition assessment
assessment: Journal protocol verifies intended Trail Making assessments and bundled odors, including eugenol for clove in conventional training. No isolated clove intake or clinical Parkinson results are reported.

fit: clove odor kit and Trail Making Test B in an HIV protocol
assessment: The recruiting study lists a conventional odor kit that includes clove and a cognitive task measuring executive performance. Results are not posted. The intervention bundles odors and has no identified ingested ground-clove or Parkinson arm.

fit: clove as one of six odorants in a diabetes cognition training trial
assessment: The original abstract reports MoCA change +1.9 versus +0.4 (p=.001) and executive-domain gains with the training package. Exact executive estimates remain open. Clove is one inhaled stimulus and the participants had diabetes with mild cognitive impairment.

fit: soybean oil comparator with measured subjective sleep quality
assessment: Soy oil VAS sleep quality was 80.8 to 80.7 over eight weeks; lysolecithin was 76.5 to 77.5. The study lacked an untreated arm, excluded sleep problems, has unreported oil refining and does not measure Parkinson daytime sleepiness. UMIN first posted after the reported follow-up.

fit: linked fetal and neonatal behavior after maternal kale powder
assessment: The 2025 report follows the same maternal capsule study as PMID36130610. Neonatal swab testing examines facial responses to odors. The study does not measure a change in adult olfactory impairment, roasted kale exposure or Parkinson outcomes.

fit: hoarseness with competing anatomical cause in one adult who ate blueberries
assessment: Hoarseness progressed despite blueberry cessation and imaging found an anterior mediastinal mass with partial tracheal compression. The case supplies no verified berry preparation, acoustic voice-volume measure, causal allergy challenge, or Parkinson cohort.
